summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar served as Principal at The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, T. V. Venkatachala Sastry held positions at Osmania University from around 1964 to 1968 and served as Professor at the University of Mysore from circa 1968 to 1994.

T. Venkatacharya was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who taught at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente and served as a Professor in East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 1971).

Tadao Yoshikawa, a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1965). He later taught at Hanazono University (~1967–1984) and held professorships at Kyoto University (~1988–2000) and Ryukoku University (~2000–2007).

Tadashi Inoue specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953). He later held posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto University of the Arts, and Nara University (~1978–1999 as professor).

Focusing on Buddhist studies and philosophy, Tadashi Tani studied at Waseda University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama. He served as professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000) and lectured at Ryukoku, Hanazono, Bukkyo, and Kobe Women's universities.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who was educated under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tadeusz Skorupski earned his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978. He later held posts at SOAS University of London as Professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.

Taido Kitamura, working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, held academic appointments at Shuchiin University, including as an assistant professor attested in 1980 and with posts attested between 1994 and 1999.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Taigen Dan Leighton earned a PhD from the Graduate Theological Union and studied with several traditional teachers. He held posts as Adjunct Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994) and taught at Loyola University Chicago (~2010).

Taiji Kuroda, specializing in Indology and philosophy, completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1971–1976). He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1986) and at Osaka Gakuin College (attested 1988).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Taijun Inokuchi served as a lecturer and committee member at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and as head of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at Japan Women's University and held an assistant professorship and subsequent post at the University of Tokyo (1912–1930).
Taiken Kyuma, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD from the University of Vienna in 1999. He later served as an Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Working in the field of Buddhist studies, Taiken Tanaka studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Taiko Yamasaki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Koyasan University as a pupil of Bokushō Kanayama. He held posts at Koyasan University and Shuchiin University.

Tainori Tanigawa, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University (1994). He served at Koyasan University as an assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor (attested 2005).
Taion Satomi specialized in Buddhist studies and completed his studies at Rissho University in 1933. He later served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).
